minted_by.pass: Native source-binding refresh; only derived spoken backs changed from the preserved draft/accepted deck; independent07/08 pending

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “A handbook cannot replace driving … develop experience and judgment.”
cards.back: A handbook cannot replace driving instruction and supervised practice needed to develop experience and judgment.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Scan ahead, beside and behind … speed or position change.”
cards.back: Scan ahead, beside and behind the vehicle to detect problems that may require a speed or position change.
cards.memory_hook: Check the view before moving.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Looking far along the intended … helping traffic flow steadily.”
cards.back: Looking far along the intended path can reduce emergency reactions and steering weave while helping traffic flow steadily.
cards.memory_hook: Check the view before moving.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “On a highway, the handbook … least a quarter-mile ahead.”
cards.back: On a highway, the handbook recommends looking at least a quarter-mile ahead.
cards.memory_hook: Check the view before moving.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Search ahead for entering or … can be made early.”
cards.back: Search ahead for entering or turning vehicles and brake lights so speed or lane changes can be made early.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “A light that has remained … and prepare to stop.”
cards.back: A light that has remained green for a long time may change before arrival; begin slowing and prepare to stop.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Early driving adjustments give following … more time to respond.”
cards.back: Early driving adjustments give following drivers more time to respond.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Measure look-ahead time by counting … object first seen ahead.”
cards.back: Measure look-ahead time by counting seconds until reaching a stationary object first seen ahead.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “The handbook defines visual lead … front of the vehicle.”
cards.back: The handbook defines visual lead as the area about twenty to thirty seconds in front of the vehicle.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “A useful visual lead helps … to stop or steer.”
cards.back: A useful visual lead helps identify changing conditions and alternative paths early enough to stop or steer.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “With good tires and brakes … to react and stop.”
cards.back: With good tires and brakes on dry pavement, the handbook's sixty miles per hour example allows about four to five seconds or three hundred fifty-nine feet to react and stop.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Under the same stated good-tire, … to react and stop.”
cards.back: Under the same stated good-tire, good-brake and dry-road conditions, its thirty miles per hour example allows about two to three seconds or one hundred twenty-three feet to react and stop.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “The handbook warns that sixty … four hundred feet ahead.”
cards.back: The handbook warns that sixty miles per hour is too fast for visibility when the driver cannot see at least four hundred feet ahead.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “The handbook cautions that thirty … one hundred fifty feet.”
cards.back: The handbook cautions that thirty miles per hour may be unsafe when the visible distance is less than one hundred fifty feet.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Search sideways for vehicles and … intersections and railroad crossings.”
cards.back: Search sideways for vehicles and pedestrians entering the path, especially at intersections and railroad crossings.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Intersections include driveways, shopping-center lanes … well as crossing streets.”
cards.back: Intersections include driveways, shopping-center lanes and parking-lot entrances as well as crossing streets.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “On intersection approach, check traffic, … views and pavement conditions.”
cards.back: On intersection approach, check traffic, road users, controls, blocked views and pavement conditions.
cards.memory_hook: Check the view before moving.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Before entering an intersection, search … right and left again.”
cards.back: Before entering an intersection, search ahead, left and right; after stopping, look left, right and left again.
cards.memory_hook: Check the view before moving.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Check cross traffic even when … the light turns green.”
cards.back: Check cross traffic even when it faces red or a stop sign, particularly immediately after the light turns green.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Enter an intersection only with … will not block it.”
cards.back: Enter an intersection only with a clear path through it and a view of crossing traffic, so a stop will not block it.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “When stopped with a blocked … until the view opens.”
cards.back: When stopped with a blocked cross-street view, edge forward slowly until the view opens.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Give extra sideways attention near … construction, playgrounds and schoolyards.”
cards.back: Give extra sideways attention near busy sidewalks, shopping areas, construction, playgrounds and schoolyards.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Before a left turn across … block the turning path.”
cards.back: Before a left turn across opposing traffic, find a safe gap and ensure vehicles or pedestrians will not block the turning path.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Before turning right, check traffic … left-turners and crossing pedestrians.”
cards.back: Before turning right, check traffic from the left, opposing left-turners and crossing pedestrians.
cards.memory_hook: Check the view before moving.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “At a railroad approach, slow … equipment before the tracks.”
cards.back: At a railroad approach, slow at the round warning sign and look both ways for trains or maintenance equipment before the tracks.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Check behind more often in … vehicles approaching too fast.”
cards.back: Check behind more often in heavy traffic to detect tailgaters and vehicles approaching too fast.
cards.memory_hook: Check the view before moving.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Rearward checks are particularly important … long or steep hill.”
cards.back: Rearward checks are particularly important before changing lanes, slowing, joining traffic or descending a long or steep hill.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Before a lane change or … or preparing to pass.”
cards.back: Before a lane change or merge, check behind and in the target lane, including vehicles already entering it or preparing to pass.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Maintain safe following space while … for a lane change.”
cards.back: Maintain safe following space while checking mirrors for a lane change.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “A blind spot is an … movement to check it.”
cards.back: A blind spot is an area the mirrors do not show; look over the shoulder toward the intended movement to check it.
cards.memory_hook: Check the view before moving.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Use repeated short checks instead … while attention is elsewhere.”
cards.back: Use repeated short checks instead of one long sideways look because traffic ahead may stop while attention is elsewhere.
cards.memory_hook: Check the view before moving.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “For a lane change, signal, … then cancel the signal.”
cards.back: For a lane change, signal, recheck toward the move, adjust speed and steer into the lane, then cancel the signal.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Check mirrors whenever slowing, especially … may not expect it.”
cards.back: Check mirrors whenever slowing, especially suddenly or at a driveway or parking space where followers may not expect it.
cards.memory_hook: Keep location with its parking rule.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “On a long or steep … large trucks and buses.”
cards.back: On a long or steep descent, watch mirrors for rapidly approaching vehicles, especially large trucks and buses.
cards.memory_hook: Check the view before moving.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Perception distance is the distance … it under ideal conditions.”
cards.back: Perception distance is the distance traveled from seeing a hazard until recognizing it under ideal conditions.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Visibility, the hazard and a … can change perception distance.”
cards.back: Visibility, the hazard and a driver's mental or physical condition can change perception distance.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “The handbook gives an alert … second to one second.”
cards.back: The handbook gives an alert driver's average perception time as three quarters of a second to one second.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Reaction distance is the ideal-condition … to a recognized hazard.”
cards.back: Reaction distance is the ideal-condition distance traveled before physically applying the brakes in response to a recognized hazard.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “The handbook gives average reaction … fifty miles per hour”
cards.back: The handbook gives average reaction time as three quarters of a second to one second and illustrates about fifty-five feet traveled at fifty miles per hour
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Braking distance is the distance … applied under ideal conditions.”
cards.back: Braking distance is the distance traveled while the brakes are being applied under ideal conditions.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “The handbook's fifty-mph dry-road example … feet of braking distance.”
cards.back: The handbook's fifty miles per hour dry-road example with good brakes gives about one hundred fifty-eight feet of braking distance.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Total stopping distance combines perception, … the vehicle fully stops.”
cards.back: Total stopping distance combines perception, reaction and braking travel until the vehicle fully stops.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “For its ideal-condition fifty-mph example, … two hundred sixty-eight feet.”
cards.back: For its ideal-condition fifty miles per hour example, the handbook gives a minimum total stopping distance of two hundred sixty-eight feet.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “The handbook compares forty miles … effect of increased speed.”
cards.back: The handbook compares forty miles per hour with twenty miles per hour as four times the impact and braking distance, illustrating the effect of increased speed.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Its sixty-mph comparison with twenty … impact and braking distance.”
cards.back: Its sixty miles per hour comparison with twenty miles per hour gives nine times the impact and braking distance.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Its eighty-mph comparison with twenty … impact and braking distance.”
cards.back: Its eighty miles per hour comparison with twenty miles per hour gives sixteen times the impact and braking distance.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Sudden slowing makes it harder … to avoid a collision.”
cards.back: Sudden slowing makes it harder for following vehicles to avoid a collision.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “To avoid panic stops, the … making needed changes early.”
cards.back: To avoid panic stops, the handbook recommends searching at least ten seconds ahead and making needed changes early.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Recall the complete rule beginning “Planning ahead and slowing gradually …”.
cards.back: Planning ahead and slowing gradually can conserve fuel.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Choose speed for traffic and … space and applicable limits.”
cards.back: Choose speed for traffic and road conditions, available forward view, following space and applicable limits.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Reduce speed before sharp curves, … be on the road.”
cards.back: Reduce speed before sharp curves, on slippery pavement and when animals may be on the road.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Slow to a safe speed … cause loss of traction.”
cards.back: Slow to a safe speed before a curve rather than braking hard after entry, which can cause loss of traction.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Reduce curve-entry speed further when … curve's end is hidden.”
cards.back: Reduce curve-entry speed further when traction is poor, when following another vehicle or when the curve's end is hidden.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “At a safe curve speed, … acceleration through the curve.”
cards.back: At a safe curve speed, the handbook calls for slight, steady acceleration through the curve.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Slow at the first signs … make the surface slippery.”
cards.back: Slow at the first signs of rain, snow or sleet because water mixes with dirt and oil to make the surface slippery.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “A sudden rain on hot … surface oil washes away.”
cards.back: A sudden rain on hot pavement may be particularly slippery during the first few minutes before surface oil washes away.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Poor grip on wet pavement … makes skid-free turning harder.”
cards.back: Poor grip on wet pavement lengthens stops and makes skid-free turning harder.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “For wet roads, the handbook … stopping and steering space.”
cards.back: For wet roads, the handbook recommends about ten miles per hour below the recommended speed to allow extra stopping and steering space.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “For packed snow, the handbook … by at least half.”
cards.back: For packed snow, the handbook recommends reducing speed by at least half.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “On ice, reduce speed to … ice-covered roads if possible.”
cards.back: On ice, reduce speed to provide extra stopping and recovery room; avoid driving on ice-covered roads if possible.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “The handbook permits studded snow … one through April one.”
cards.back: The handbook permits studded snow tires in Kansas from November one through April one.
cards.memory_hook: Keep the licensing path distinct.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “A road's crown and drainage … vehicle toward the roadside.”
cards.back: A road's crown and drainage slope can carry a skidding vehicle toward the roadside.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Shaded pavement on cold wet … areas and dry later.”
cards.back: Shaded pavement on cold wet days can freeze before other areas and dry later.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Bridge, overpass and underpass pavement … nearby roads are clear.”
cards.back: Bridge, overpass and underpass pavement may be icy even when nearby roads are clear.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Near freezing, liquid water over … at much colder temperatures.”
cards.back: Near freezing, liquid water over ice can make the surface more slippery than ice at much colder temperatures.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride … contact with the pavement.”
cards.back: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on pooled water and lose contact with the pavement.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Slow in rain and on … to reduce hydroplaning risk.”
cards.back: Slow in rain and on wet roads with puddles to reduce hydroplaning risk.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Driving faster than the traffic … pace within legal limits.”
cards.back: Driving faster than the traffic stream creates repeated passing conflicts; keep pace within legal limits.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “The handbook warns that driving … bunching and passing attempts.”
cards.back: The handbook warns that driving over fifteen miles per hour below the traffic stream can create dangerous bunching and passing attempts.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “If traffic bunches behind a … and let others pass.”
cards.back: If traffic bunches behind a slow vehicle, its driver should pull over when safe and let others pass.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “On an entrance ramp, check … and obey ramp-speed signs.”
cards.back: On an entrance ramp, check destination and route signs and obey ramp-speed signs.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Use an acceleration lane to … joining the main roadway.”
cards.back: Use an acceleration lane to approach traffic speed before joining the main roadway.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Avoid reaching the end of … the lane while waiting.”
cards.back: Avoid reaching the end of an acceleration lane and stopping; if a gap is unavailable, slow within the lane while waiting.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Do not cross the solid … from an acceleration lane.”
cards.back: Do not cross the solid white boundary when joining from an acceleration lane.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Before joining the roadway, check … when a gap opens.”
cards.back: Before joining the roadway, check mirrors and over the shoulder toward the move; signal and enter carefully when a gap opens.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “In heavy traffic, the handbook … mile before the exit.”
cards.back: In heavy traffic, the handbook recommends reaching the exit lane about half a mile before the exit.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “For an exit with a … after entering that lane.”
cards.back: For an exit with a deceleration lane, maintain speed on the main roadway and reduce it after entering that lane.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “When exiting a limited-access road, … regard to vehicles ahead.”
cards.back: When exiting a limited-access road, check the ramp speed and following traffic before slowing, and brake with regard to vehicles ahead.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Reduce speed in crowded places … and busy downtown streets.”
cards.back: Reduce speed in crowded places where maneuvering room is limited, including shopping areas and busy downtown streets.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Heavy rush-hour traffic, narrow bridges, … space and changing movements.”
cards.back: Heavy rush-hour traffic, narrow bridges, tunnels and toll plazas can require lower speed for limited space and changing movements.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Near schools, playgrounds and residential … entering the road unexpectedly.”
cards.back: Near schools, playgrounds and residential streets, watch for children entering the road unexpectedly.
cards.memory_hook: Match protection to the occupant.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “At railroad crossings, check for … levels may require slowing.”
cards.back: At railroad crossings, check for trains and room to clear; uneven crossing levels may require slowing.
cards.memory_hook: Check the view before moving.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Excess speed reduces maneuvering ability … distance traveled while reacting.”
cards.back: Excess speed reduces maneuvering ability and increases the distance traveled while reacting.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Higher speed can reduce barrier … and increase collision severity.”
cards.back: Higher speed can reduce barrier protection and increase collision severity.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “The handbook identifies added tire … others as speed-related risks.”
cards.back: The handbook identifies added tire and brake wear, driver fatigue and harder distance judgments by others as speed-related risks.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “For normal conditions without special … for an urban district.”
cards.back: For normal conditions without special hazards or a different posted limit, the handbook gives thirty miles per hour for an urban district.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “The handbook specifies a two-second … traffic or weather conditions.”
cards.back: The handbook specifies a two-second minimum following interval, adding a second for unusual traffic or weather conditions.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “A posted speed assumes ideal … visibility or heavy traffic.”
cards.back: A posted speed assumes ideal conditions; slow for wet or icy pavement, poor visibility or heavy traffic.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “A posted fifty-five-mph limit does … appropriate during a snowstorm.”
cards.back: A posted fifty-five miles per hour limit does not make fifty-five miles per hour appropriate during a snowstorm.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Check the speedometer frequently, especially … to a slower road.”
cards.back: Check the speedometer frequently, especially after moving from a fast multilane road to a slower road.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “High-center-of-gravity vehicles are more prone … and slow before curves.”
cards.back: High-center-of-gravity vehicles are more prone to rollover; drive at a suitable lower speed, avoid abrupt direction changes and slow before curves.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “ABS means Anti-Lock Braking System … without upsetting vehicle balance.”
cards.back: ABS means Anti-Lock Braking System and is intended to permit steering while braking without upsetting vehicle balance.
cards.memory_hook: Keep the licensing path distinct.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “ABS does not necessarily shorten … generally shortens wet-surface stops.”
cards.back: ABS does not necessarily shorten dry-road stops, though the handbook says it generally shortens wet-surface stops.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “For ABS use, the handbook … steer toward that space.”
cards.back: For ABS use, the handbook directs the driver to find open space, press the brake firmly and steer toward that space.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Use the owner's manual to … a vehicle has ABS.”
cards.back: Use the owner's manual to establish whether a vehicle has ABS.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “The ABS indicator normally illuminates … on indicates a malfunction.”
cards.back: The ABS indicator normally illuminates at startup and then goes out; a light that stays on indicates a malfunction.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “ESP means Electronic Stability Program; … the vehicle's actual movement.”
cards.back: ESP means Electronic Stability Program; it compares the driver's steering request with the vehicle's actual movement.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “ESP can apply individual brakes … to help reduce skidding.”
cards.back: ESP can apply individual brakes when it detects a traction-related mismatch to help reduce skidding.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “During traction loss with ESP, … and avoid abrupt steering.”
cards.back: During traction loss with ESP, steer toward the intended path and avoid abrupt steering.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “A space cushion gives more … to other road users.”
cards.back: A space cushion gives more time to react to other road users.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Check following time by counting … seconds is too close.”
cards.back: Check following time by counting from when the vehicle ahead clears a fixed marker until the following vehicle reaches it; fewer than two seconds is too close.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “If following too closely, slow … at least two seconds.”
cards.back: If following too closely, slow down and repeat the fixed-marker count until the interval is at least two seconds.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Slippery roads may require more … basic two-second following interval.”
cards.back: Slippery roads may require more than the basic two-second following interval.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “When a following driver wants … shorten the passing maneuver.”
cards.back: When a following driver wants to pass, slow to create more room ahead and shorten the passing maneuver.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Leave extra space behind motorcycles … or a fallen rider.”
cards.back: Leave extra space behind motorcycles for differing braking performance or a fallen rider.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Increase following space behind vehicles … driver can see ahead.”
cards.back: Increase following space behind vehicles with blocked rear views so their drivers can see the following vehicle and its driver can see ahead.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Carry a larger front cushion … and steering ability decreases.”
cards.back: Carry a larger front cushion when hauling a heavy load or towing a trailer because stopping takes longer and steering ability decreases.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Increase following space in darkness … reduces the forward view.”
cards.back: Increase following space in darkness or bad weather that reduces the forward view.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “When tailgated, increase the space … can be less abrupt.”
cards.back: When tailgated, increase the space ahead so braking or steering can be less abrupt.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Recall the complete rule beginning “Give emergency vehicles additional following …”.
cards.back: Give emergency vehicles additional following space to operate.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Leave extra room behind vehicles … buses and hazardous-material carriers.”
cards.back: Leave extra room behind vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, such as buses and hazardous-material carriers.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Leave extra space when stopped … backward before moving ahead.”
cards.back: Leave extra space when stopped behind another vehicle on an incline because it may roll backward before moving ahead.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Steady speed, early signals and … maintain a safe gap.”
cards.back: Steady speed, early signals and extra front space before slowing can help a following driver maintain a safe gap.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “When tailgated and an empty … the other vehicle pass.”
cards.back: When tailgated and an empty lane is available, move into it to let the other vehicle pass.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “If tailgated without an empty … to encourage a pass.”
cards.back: If tailgated without an empty lane, wait for a clear road ahead and then slow gradually to encourage a pass.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Do not brake sharply to … rear-end and aggressive-driving risks.”
cards.back: Do not brake sharply to discourage a tailgater; it raises rear-end and aggressive-driving risks.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “The handbook recommends adding two … being followed too closely.”
cards.back: The handbook recommends adding two to three seconds to the front following interval when being followed too closely.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Avoid staying beside another vehicle … to preserve lateral room.”
cards.back: Avoid staying beside another vehicle on a multilane road; adjust speed to preserve lateral room.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “On a two-way road, avoid … to evade either way.”
cards.back: On a two-way road, avoid crowding the centerline; the lane center generally leaves room to evade either way.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Make room for merging traffic … that lane is clear.”
cards.back: Make room for merging traffic by moving to the next lane when that lane is clear.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Leave extra room beside parked … may enter the path.”
cards.back: Leave extra room beside parked cars without crossing the centerline because doors, people or vehicles may enter the path.
cards.memory_hook: Keep location with its parking rule.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Give pedestrians and cyclists, particularly … space for unexpected movement.”
cards.back: Give pedestrians and cyclists, particularly children, additional space for unexpected movement.
cards.memory_hook: Match protection to the occupant.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “When a tractor-trailer passes, moving … remaining within the lane.”
cards.back: When a tractor-trailer passes, moving toward the outside of the lane can increase separation while remaining within the lane.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Select a merge gap that … into a small opening.”
cards.back: Select a merge gap that leaves time to establish a suitable following interval rather than forcing into a small opening.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Cross multiple lanes one at … and can create conflicts.”
cards.back: Cross multiple lanes one at a time because checking several at once is difficult and can create conflicts.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “After stopping before crossing traffic, … three to five seconds.”
cards.back: After stopping before crossing traffic, allow enough gap to get fully across; the handbook's normal-condition example is about three to five seconds.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “When entering traffic with a … turn and to accelerate.”
cards.back: When entering traffic with a turn, allow room both to complete the turn and to accelerate.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “The handbook's normal-condition right-turn-and-acceleration example … twelve to fifteen seconds.”
cards.back: The handbook's normal-condition right-turn-and-acceleration example takes about twelve to fifteen seconds.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Its normal-condition left-turn-and-acceleration example takes … fifteen to eighteen seconds.”
cards.back: Its normal-condition left-turn-and-acceleration example takes about fifteen to eighteen seconds.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Do not begin crossing even … block the exit path.”
cards.back: Do not begin crossing even on green if vehicles block the exit path.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Before a left turn, confirm … in the opposing path.”
cards.back: Before a left turn, confirm that neither vehicles nor pedestrians will trap the vehicle in the opposing path.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Do not enter merely because … a genuinely safe gap.”
cards.back: Do not enter merely because another driver's turn signal is on; wait for the turn to begin and a genuinely safe gap.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Another vehicle's signal may indicate … it does not self-cancel.”
cards.back: Another vehicle's signal may indicate a later turn or may have been left on accidentally, especially if it does not self-cancel.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Cross railroad tracks only when … without stopping on them.”
cards.back: Cross railroad tracks only when there is room to clear without stopping on them.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Complete a pass as promptly … time beside another vehicle.”
cards.back: Complete a pass as promptly as safety permits to limit time beside another vehicle.
cards.memory_hook: Keep the licensing path distinct.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Before passing, check oncoming traffic, … the rear blind spot.”
cards.back: Before passing, check oncoming traffic, side-road entries and slowing vehicles ahead, as well as mirrors and the rear blind spot.
cards.memory_hook: Check the view before moving.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Signal a safe pass and … the vehicle being overtaken.”
cards.back: Signal a safe pass and begin from at least two seconds behind the vehicle being overtaken.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Steer smoothly into the passing … toward the passed vehicle.”
cards.back: Steer smoothly into the passing lane, keep checking ahead and in mirrors, and avoid drifting toward the passed vehicle.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Before returning after a pass, … signal and return smoothly.”
cards.back: Before returning after a pass, see the entire front of the passed vehicle in the rearview mirror, then signal and return smoothly.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “When being passed, move toward … maintain a steady speed.”
cards.back: When being passed, move toward the right side of the lane and maintain a steady speed.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Passing permission from signs or … requires enough safe space.”
cards.back: Passing permission from signs or markings still requires enough safe space.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “The handbook recommends passing one … twenty to thirty seconds.”
cards.back: The handbook recommends passing one vehicle at a time and warns that a pass can take as long as twenty to thirty seconds.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Do not attempt a pass … distance is uncertain, wait.”
cards.back: Do not attempt a pass when an oncoming vehicle is visible; if time or distance is uncertain, wait.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Oncoming vehicles can appear slower … making passing-distance judgment difficult.”
cards.back: Oncoming vehicles can appear slower than their actual closing speed, making passing-distance judgment difficult.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “The handbook's perception warning says … than twenty-five seconds remains.”
cards.back: The handbook's perception warning says a vehicle more than twenty-five seconds away may look stationary; visible closing motion may mean less than twenty-five seconds remains.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “For passing near hills or … twenty to twenty-five seconds.”
cards.back: For passing near hills or curves at fifty-five to sixty miles per hour, the handbook calls for at least one-third mile of forward view, about twenty to twenty-five seconds.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Treat a hill or curve … one-third mile of it.”
cards.back: Treat a hill or curve that blocks the view as hiding opposing traffic and do not start passing within one-third mile of it.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Do not pass in intersections, … alleys or parking entrances.”
cards.back: Do not pass in intersections, and avoid passing at other crossing points such as driveways, alleys or parking entrances.
cards.memory_hook: Keep location with its parking rule.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Before a pass, look for … force another vehicle sideways.”
cards.back: Before a pass, look for pedestrians, cyclists, narrow bridges, ice, potholes or obstructions that may force another vehicle sideways.
cards.memory_hook: Check the view before moving.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Do not pass without room … drivers creating that room.”
cards.back: Do not pass without room to return to the travel lane, and do not depend on other drivers creating that room.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “The handbook advises against passing … twenty-five seconds of travel.”
cards.back: The handbook advises against passing with a railroad crossing in the next twenty to twenty-five seconds of travel.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Allow extra space for drivers … backing into the road.”
cards.back: Allow extra space for drivers whose view is blocked at intersections or driveways and for drivers backing into the road.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Give extra room to people … umbrellas or lowered hats.”
cards.back: Give extra room to people whose vision is obstructed by icy windows, umbrellas or lowered hats.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Use additional caution or space … workers and inattentive pedestrians.”
cards.back: Use additional caution or space around distracted people such as delivery workers, construction workers and inattentive pedestrians.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Allow for confused drivers who … for directions or addresses.”
cards.back: Allow for confused drivers who slow unexpectedly or search for directions or addresses.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “If a passing driver runs … that vehicle return safely.”
cards.back: If a passing driver runs short of space, slow down to help that vehicle return safely.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “If another driver needs an … merge can reduce conflict.”
cards.back: If another driver needs an abrupt lane change, slowing to let that driver merge can reduce conflict.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Handle hazards separately when possible; … vehicle has gone by.”
cards.back: Handle hazards separately when possible; delay passing a roadside pedestrian until an opposing vehicle has gone by.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Communicating location and intended movement … anticipate the vehicle's actions.”
cards.back: Communicating location and intended movement helps other road users anticipate the vehicle's actions.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Use headlights to improve the … or fog reduces visibility.”
cards.back: Use headlights to improve the vehicle's visibility to others, especially when rain, snow or fog reduces visibility.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “The handbook states that Kansas … vehicle's wipers are used.”
cards.back: The handbook states that Kansas requires headlights whenever the vehicle's wipers are used.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Switch on headlights as daylight … drivers see the vehicle.”
cards.back: Switch on headlights as daylight fades; doing so slightly early helps other drivers see the vehicle.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Use headlights while driving away … drivers see the vehicle.”
cards.back: Use headlights while driving away from a low rising or setting sun to help opposing drivers see the vehicle.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Keep headlights clean and working … visibility without dazzling others.”
cards.back: Keep headlights clean and working and have a qualified person check their aim to preserve visibility without dazzling others.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “A horn can warn of … to strike one another.”
cards.back: A horn can warn of an imminent collision, including a pedestrian entering the street or vehicles about to strike one another.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Do not use the horn … driver to move faster.”
cards.back: Do not use the horn to greet someone, complain about an error or pressure a driver to move faster.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Recall the complete rule beginning “Avoid sounding the horn near …”.
cards.back: Avoid sounding the horn near a blind pedestrian.
cards.memory_hook: Check the view before moving.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “If possible during a breakdown, … give an emergency number.”
cards.back: If possible during a breakdown, notify authorities by phone or another device; roadside signs may give an emergency number.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “For a breakdown stop, move … the road when possible.”
cards.back: For a breakdown stop, move away from traffic and off the road when possible.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Turn on hazard flashers to … indicate a disabled vehicle.”
cards.back: Turn on hazard flashers to indicate a disabled vehicle.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Choose a breakdown stopping place … a hillcrest or bend.”
cards.back: Choose a breakdown stopping place visible to approaching users rather than just beyond a hillcrest or bend.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “The handbook describes placing warning … to alert approaching drivers.”
cards.back: The handbook describes placing warning flares about two hundred to three hundred feet behind a disabled vehicle to alert approaching drivers.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Do not remain in the … within a traffic lane.”
cards.back: Do not remain in the roadway or attempt a tire change within a traffic lane.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “A white cloth on the … indicate a disabled vehicle.”
cards.back: A white cloth on the antenna, mirror or door handle, or a raised hood, can indicate a disabled vehicle.
cards.memory_hook: Check the view before moving.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Signal changes in direction or … can anticipate the movement.”
cards.back: Signal changes in direction or slowing so other road users can anticipate the movement.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Use turn signals before intersection … lane changes or merges.”
cards.back: Use turn signals before intersection turns and the lane-change signal function for lane changes or merges.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “After a turn or lane … it off if necessary.”
cards.back: After a turn or lane change, check that the signal has canceled and switch it off if necessary.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Brake lights communicate slowing; reduce … early as safely possible.”
cards.back: Brake lights communicate slowing; reduce speed as early as safely possible.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “When slowing unexpectedly, the handbook … to warn following traffic.”
cards.back: When slowing unexpectedly, the handbook recommends three or four light brake-pedal taps to warn following traffic.
cards.memory_hook: Match the space to conditions.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Warn before slowing to turn … exit or turn lane.”
cards.back: Warn before slowing to turn off a road without a separate exit or turn lane.
cards.memory_hook: Read the control and its condition.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Warn before parking or turning … continued travel through it.”
cards.back: Warn before parking or turning before an intersection when followers may expect continued travel through it.
cards.memory_hook: Keep location with its parking rule.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Warn before slowing for a … close follower cannot see.”
cards.back: Warn before slowing for a hidden hazard or traffic queue that a close follower cannot see.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “A driver's license is a … rather than a right.”
cards.back: A driver's license is a privilege rather than a right.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Recall the complete rule beginning “Drive without drug, alcohol …”.
cards.back: Drive without drug, alcohol or other impairment.
cards.memory_hook: Check readiness before driving.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “The driver and passengers should … always wear seat belts.”
cards.back: The driver and passengers should always wear seat belts.
cards.memory_hook: Match protection to the occupant.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “A minor and the minor's … of the minor's driving.”
cards.back: A minor and the minor's parent or guardian bear financial consequences of the minor's driving.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Drivers are responsible for parking … vehicle from rolling away.”
cards.back: Drivers are responsible for parking without obstructing traffic or pedestrians and preventing the vehicle from rolling away.
cards.memory_hook: Keep location with its parking rule.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Courtesy helps address situations that … do not explicitly cover.”
cards.back: Courtesy helps address situations that traffic rules do not explicitly cover.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Assess personal driving limitations, vehicle … as sources of risk.”
cards.back: Assess personal driving limitations, vehicle limitations and road or weather conditions as sources of risk.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Large vehicles may be less … for others to see.”
cards.back: Large vehicles may be less stable with restricted surrounding visibility, while small vehicles may be harder for others to see.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Manage identified risks through position … but not completely eliminated.”
cards.back: Manage identified risks through position and speed changes; risks can be reduced but not completely eliminated.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Position or speed changes can … and separate conflicting hazards.”
cards.back: Position or speed changes can increase response time, improve control and separate conflicting hazards.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Recall the complete rule beginning “Driving decisions improve with …”.
cards.back: Driving decisions improve with practice and experience.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Begin decisions with an active … positions and their paths.”
cards.back: Begin decisions with an active search for other users, their positions and their paths.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “After identifying road users, assess … collide with the vehicle.”
cards.back: After identifying road users, assess their movement and whether they could collide with the vehicle.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Responses can include changes in … after choosing the response.”
cards.back: Responses can include changes in speed, changes in direction and communication; take action after choosing the response.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Practice anticipating a possible hazard, … risk and then acting.”
cards.back: Practice anticipating a possible hazard, deciding how to reduce its risk and then acting.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.

cards.front: Complete this rule in full: “Rehearsing possible situations with what-if … prepare for rapid decisions.”
cards.back: Rehearsing possible situations with what-if questions can help prepare for rapid decisions.
cards.memory_hook: Keep this condition with its action.
